question: Which facial bones contain the maxillary sinuses?
explanation: The maxillary sinuses are located within the maxillary bones, which form the structure of the cheekbones. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T3#BMP125_U1_T3_h1)

question: What is the primary job of the tiny cilia inside the sinuses?

options.C: Sweep mucus out into the nose
options.D: Warm the air entering the lungs

explanation: Cilia act like tiny brooms, constantly moving to clear mucus out of the sinus cavities and into the nasal passages. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T3#BMP125_U1_T3_h1)

question: How long must sinus symptoms last to be classified as chronic sinusitis?
explanation: Chronic sinusitis is defined by inflammation that persists for longer than three months, or twelve weeks. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T3#BMP125_U1_T3_h2)

question: What main physical event starts the process of sinusitis inside the sinus cavity?

options.D: Drying out of all body fluids

explanation: When the tiny drainage opening, or ostium, gets blocked, mucus cannot escape, which sets off the cycle of infection and pressure. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T3#BMP125_U1_T3_h2)

question: Which action makes facial pain and pressure worse for a patient with sinusitis?
explanation: Bending forward increases gravity-induced pressure against the congested, inflamed walls of the blocked sinuses. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T3#BMP125_U1_T3_h3)

question: A patient complains of throbbing pain in the upper teeth and cheeks. Which sinuses are most likely affected?
explanation: The roots of the upper teeth sit very close to the floor of the maxillary sinuses, making upper dental pain a classic sign of maxillary sinusitis. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T3#BMP125_U1_T3_h3)

question: What is considered the gold standard imaging test for viewing the paranasal sinuses?
explanation: A CT scan provides the clearest pictures of the bone structures and fluid collections inside the sinuses. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T3#BMP125_U1_T3_h4)

question: Why are most cases of uncomplicated acute sinusitis diagnosed without a CT scan?

options.A: Government rules forbid scanning the head
options.B: Clinical history and physical exam are usually enough
options.C: X-rays are much cheaper and safer to use
options.D: CT scans cannot detect sinus infections at all

explanation: A thorough health history and physical assessment provide enough clear signs to start treatment for standard acute sinusitis. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T3#BMP125_U1_T3_h4)

question: What is the main danger of using over-the-counter nasal decongestant sprays for longer than five days?
explanation: Using decongestant sprays for too long causes the blood vessels in the nose to swell up even worse when the medicine wears off. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T3#BMP125_U1_T3_h5)

question: Why should antibiotics NOT be prescribed immediately for every patient who presents with sinus symptoms?

options.A: Most acute cases are caused by viruses
options.B: Bacterial infections never happen in sinuses
options.C: Antibiotics make facial pain much worse
options.D: Pills are too hard for adults to swallow

explanation: Since the vast majority of early sinus infections are viral, antibiotics will not cure them and can contribute to drug resistance. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T3#BMP125_U1_T3_h5)

question: What is a major reason for encouraging a patient with sinusitis to drink plenty of water?

options.A: To prevent the kidneys from failing
options.B: To cool down body temperature fast
options.C: To thin out thick mucus secretions
options.D: To stop the stomach from cramping

explanation: Adequate hydration is a simple, highly effective way to make sticky mucus thinner and easier for the sinuses to drain. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T3#BMP125_U1_T3_h6)

question: A patient preparing a home nasal saline rinse asks what kind of water is safest to use. What should the midwife advise?
explanation: Using sterile, or boiled and cooled tap water, prevents introducing harmful microorganisms directly into vulnerable nasal sinuses. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T3#BMP125_U1_T3_h6)

question: Why can a sinus infection sometimes spread to the eye socket or the brain?

options.A: Blood flows backward away from the head during rest
options.B: Sinus bones dissolve completely during an infection
options.C: Bacteria can fly through the air inside the skull
options.D: The sinuses sit very close to the eyes and brain

explanation: The paranasal sinuses are located right next to the eye sockets and the skull cavity, allowing severe infections to spread to nearby areas. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T3#BMP125_U1_T3_h7)

question: Which symptom in a patient with sinusitis requires IMMEDIATE emergency medical attention?

options.A: Scratchy throat when swallowing warm tea
options.B: A slight loss of taste for favorite foods
options.C: Mild tiredness after a full night of sleep
options.D: Changes in vision and swelling around the eye

explanation: Visual changes and periorbital swelling suggest the infection has spread into the eye socket, which is a medical emergency. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T3#BMP125_U1_T3_h7)
